lines: Financial regulators in Britain have imposed a rather unusual rule on the bosses of big banks. Starting next year, any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing. The main purpose of this "**clawback**" rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions. Yet officials also hope for a much larger benefit: more long-term decision-making, not only by banks but by all corporations, to build a stronger economy for future **generations**.
英国的金融监管机构对大银行的高管们实施了一项颇为罕见的规则。从明年起，如果银行正因不当行为接受调查，其高管的任何保底奖金都可能被递延十年。这项“追回”规则的主要目的，是让银行家对有害的冒险行为承担责任，并恢复公众对金融机构的信任。然而官员们还期望更大的收益：不仅银行，所有企业都能作出更多的长期决策，为子孙后代建设更强大的经济。

lines: "**Short-termism**," or the desire for quick profits, has worsened in publicly traded companies, says the Bank of England's top economist, Andrew Haldane. He quotes a giant of classical economics, Alfred Marshall, in describing this financial impatience as acting like "children who pick the plums out of their pudding to eat them at once" rather than putting them aside to be eaten last. The average time for holding a stock in both the United States and Britain, he notes, has dropped from seven years to seven months in recent decades. **Transient** investors, who demand high quarterly profits from companies, can hinder a firm's efforts to invest in long-term research or to build up customer loyalty. This has been dubbed "quarterly capitalism."

英格兰银行首席经济学家安德鲁·霍尔丹表示，“短期主义”，即对快钱的渴望，在上市公司中已愈演愈烈。他引用古典经济学巨擘阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔的话，把这种金融上的急不可耐比作“把布丁里的李子挑出来立刻吃掉”的孩子，而不是把李子留到最后再吃。他指出，近几十年来，美国和英国持有一只股票的平均时间已从七年缩短到七个月。那些要求公司提供高额季度利润的短线投资者，会妨碍企业投资长期研究或培养客户忠诚度的努力。这被称为“季度资本主义”。

lines: Grade inflation — the gradual increase in average GPAs (grade-point averages) over the past few decades — is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education, in which students are treated like customers to be pleased. But another, related force — a policy often buried deep in course catalogs called "grade **forgiveness**" — is helping raise GPAs.

lines: The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years, as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates. When this practice first started decades ago, it was usually limited to **freshmen**, to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses. But now most colleges, save for many selective campuses, allow all undergraduates, and even graduate students, to get their low grades forgiven.

lines: That said, there is a way in which grade forgiveness satisfies colleges' own needs as well. For public institutions, state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on **metrics** such as graduation rates and student retention — so better grades can, by boosting figures like those, mean more money. And anything that raises GPAs will likely make students — who, at the end of the day, are paying the bill — feel they've gotten a better value for their tuition dollars, which is another big concern for colleges.

lines: States will be able to force more people to pay sales tax when they make online purchases under a Supreme Court decision Thursday that will leave shoppers with lighter wallets but is a big financial win for states.
根据最高法院周四的一项裁定，各州将能够强制更多人在网购时缴纳销售税。这一裁定会让购物者的钱包更瘪，但却是各州的一次重大财政胜利。

lines: The Supreme Court's opinion Thursday overruled a pair of decades-old decisions that states said cost them billions of dollars in lost revenue annually. The decisions made it more difficult for states to collect sales tax on certain online purchases.
最高法院周四的意见推翻了两项延续数十年的裁决——各州声称这些裁决使它们每年损失数十亿美元的收入。这些裁决使各州更难以对某些网购征收销售税。

lines: The cases the court overturned said that if a business was shipping a customer's purchase to a state where the business didn't have a **physical** presence such as a warehouse or office, the business didn't have to collect sales tax for the state. Customers were generally responsible for paying the sales tax to the state themselves if they weren't charged it, but most didn't realize they owed it and few paid.
被推翻的那两个案例认定：如果企业把顾客购买的商品寄往一个它并无仓库或办公室等实体存在的州，该企业就无须为该州代收销售税。若未被征收，顾客原则上应自行向州政府缴纳销售税，但大多数人并未意识到自己有此义务，实际缴纳者寥寥。

lines: Justice Anthony Kennedy wrote that the previous decisions were flawed. "Each year the physical presence rule becomes further removed from economic reality and results in significant revenue losses to the States," he wrote in an opinion joined by four other justices. Kennedy wrote that the rule "limited States' ability to seek long-term prosperity and has prevented market participants from competing on an even playing field."
大法官安东尼·肯尼迪写道，以往的裁决存在缺陷。“实体存在规则年复一年地远离经济现实，给各州造成可观的税收损失，”他在一份由另外四位大法官联署的意见书中写道。肯尼迪还写道，该规则“限制了各州谋求长期繁荣的能力，并使市场参与者无法在公平的赛场上竞争”。

lines: The ruling is a victory for big chains with a presence in many states, since they usually collect sales tax on online purchases already. Now, rivals will be charging sales tax where they hadn't before. Big chains have been collecting sales tax nationwide because they typically have physical stores in whatever state a purchase is being shipped to. Amazon.com, with its network of warehouses, also collects sales tax in every state that charges it, though third-party sellers who use the site don't have to.
这一裁定是在多个州设有实体的大型连锁企业的胜利，因为它们通常已对网购代收销售税。如今，竞争对手也将在过去未征税的地方开始征税。大型连锁企业之所以在全国范围内代收销售税，是因为无论商品寄往哪个州，它们一般都在该州设有实体商店。亚马逊凭借其仓库网络，也在每个开征此税的州代收销售税，尽管使用其平台的第三方卖家并无此义务。

lines: Until now, many sellers that have a physical presence in only a single state or a few states have been able to avoid charging sales taxes when they ship to addresses outside those states. Sellers that use eBay and Etsy, which provide platforms for smaller sellers, also haven't been collecting sales tax nationwide. Under the ruling Thursday, states can pass laws requiring out-of-state sellers to collect the state's sales tax from customers and send it to the state.
在此之前，许多仅在一州或数州有实体存在的卖家，向这些州以外的地址发货时都可以不代收销售税。使用eBay和Etsy——这两个为小型卖家提供平台——的卖家，同样没有在全国范围内代收销售税。根据周四的裁定，各州可以立法要求外州卖家向顾客代收本州销售税并上缴州政府。

lines: Retail trade groups praised the ruling, saying it levels the playing field for local and online businesses. lines: (42) ______ [D] Carnegie would be right if arguments were fights, which is how we often think of them. Like physical fights, verbal fights can leave both sides bloodied. Even when you win, you end up no better off. Your prospects would be almost as dismal if arguments were even just competitions — like, say, tennis games. Pairs of opponents hit the ball back and forth until one winner emerges from all who entered. Everybody else loses. This kind of thinking is why so many people try to avoid arguments, especially about politics and religion.
(42) ______ [D] 如果争论就是打斗——我们往往就是这样看待它的——那么卡耐基说得就对了。就像肢体打斗一样，言语交锋也会让双方伤痕累累。即便赢了，到头来你的处境也不会更好。哪怕争论只是比赛，比如网球赛，你的前景也几乎同样黯淡。对手两两交锋，把球来回击打，直到所有参赛者中决出一名赢家。其他人全都输了。正是这种想法，使许多人试图避免争论，尤其是有关政治和宗教的争论。

lines: [F] These views of arguments also undermine reason. If you see a conversation as a fight or competition, you can win by cheating as long as you don't get caught. You will be happy to convince people with bad arguments. You can call their views stupid, or joke about how ignorant they are. None of these tricks will help you understand them, their positions or the issues that divide you, but they can help you win — in one way.

lines: (43) ______ [G] There is a better way to win arguments. Imagine that you favor increasing the minimum wage in our state, and I do not. If you yell, "Yes," and I yell, "No," neither of us learns anything. We neither understand nor respect each other, and we have no basis for compromise or cooperation. In contrast, suppose you give a reasonable argument: that full-time workers should not have to live in poverty. Then I counter with another reasonable argument: that a higher minimum wage will force businesses to employ fewer people for less time. Now we can understand each other's positions and recognize our shared values, since we both care about needy workers.

(43) ______ [G] 赢得争论还有一种更好的方式。设想你赞成提高本州的最低工资，而我不赞成。如果你喊“赞成”，我喊“反对”，我们谁也学不到任何东西。我们既不理解也不尊重彼此，更没有妥协或合作的基础。相反，假设你提出一个合理的论据：全职劳动者不应生活在贫困中。接着，我用另一个合理的论据反驳：最低工资提高，会迫使企业雇用更少的人，并缩短他们的工作时间。现在，我们就能理解彼此的立场，并认识到共同的价值观，因为我们都关心贫困的劳动者。

lines: It was only after I started to write a weekly column about the medical journals, and began to read scientific papers from beginning to end, that I realised just how bad much of the medical literature frequently was. I came to recognise various signs of a bad paper: the kind of paper that purports to show that people who eat more than one kilo of broccoli a week were 1.17 times more likely than those who eat less to suffer late in life from **pernicious** anaemia. (46) There is a great deal of this kind of nonsense in the medical journals which, when taken up by broadcasters and the lay press, generates both health scares and short-lived dietary enthusiasms.
直到我开始为医学期刊撰写每周专栏、开始从头到尾通读科学论文之后，我才意识到相当一部分医学文献的质量何其糟糕。我逐渐学会辨认劣质论文的种种迹象：这类论文自诩能够证明，每周吃超过一公斤西兰花的人晚年患恶性贫血的几率是吃得较少者的1.17倍。(46) 医学期刊上充斥着大量此类无稽之谈，而这些说法一经广播公司和大众媒体采用，便会同时引发健康恐慌和昙花一现的饮食时尚。

lines: Why is so much bad science published? A recent paper, titled "The Natural Selection of Bad Science", published on the Royal Society's open science website, attempts to answer this intriguing and important question. It says that the problem is not merely that people do bad science, but that our current system of career advancement positively encourages it. What is important is not truth, but publication, which has become almost an end in itself. There has been a kind of inflationary process at work: (47) nowadays anyone applying for a research post has to have published twice the number of papers that would have been required for the same post only 10 years ago. Never mind the quality, then, count the number.

为什么如此多的劣质科学得以发表？最近发表在英国皇家学会开放科学网站上的一篇题为《坏科学的自然选择》的论文，试图回答这个引人入胜而又至关重要的问题。论文指出，问题不仅在于有人在从事劣质科学研究，还在于我们现行的职业晋升体系实际上在鼓励这种行为。重要的不是真理，而是发表——发表本身几乎已成为目的。其中有一种类似通货膨胀的过程在起作用：(47) 如今，任何申请研究职位的人都必须发表论文，其数量是仅仅十年前申请同一职位所需的两倍。于是，质量不在话下，只管数数就行。

lines: (48) Attempts have been made to curb this tendency, for example, by trying to incorporate some measure of quality as well as quantity into the assessment of an applicant's papers. This is the famed **citation** index, that is to say the number of times a paper has been quoted elsewhere in the scientific literature, the assumption being that an important paper will be cited more often than one of small account. (49) This would be reasonable if it were not for the fact that scientists can easily arrange to cite themselves in their future publications, or get associates to do so for them in return for similar favours.
(48) 人们已经作出努力来遏制这种倾向，例如试图在对申请者论文的评估中，把某种衡量质量的尺度与数量一并纳入考量。这就是大名鼎鼎的引文指数，也就是说，一篇论文在科学文献其他地方被引用的次数——其假设是：重要的论文会比无足轻重的论文得到更多引用。(49) 假如不存在这样的事实——科学家可以轻而易举地安排在自己的后续论著中引用自己，或者让同事代为引用以换取同样的关照——那么这样做本是合理的。

data.image_desc: 一幅题为'途中'的漫画：两名登山者背着行囊攀登山路。其中一人瘫坐在石阶上，疲惫地抱怨自己再也爬不动了；另一人则继续坚定地向上攀登，表示绝不放弃。
sample: In the cartoon entitled "On the Way," two hikers with heavy backpacks are climbing a rugged mountain path. Exhausted, one of them sits on a stone step, complaining that he can go no further; the other, wiping his sweat, keeps climbing upward steadily, saying that he will never give up.

sample: The cartoon reveals a profound truth: on the journey of life, success belongs to those who persevere. The road to any worthwhile goal is long and steep, and fatigue and setbacks are inevitable. What separates achievers from dreamers is precisely the choice made at such moments — to sit down and surrender, or to stand up and press on. As the old saying goes, "Perseverance spells success; giving up means failure." Many great undertakings in history failed not because they were impossible, but because their pursuers stopped halfway.
